question: In round 5's PT_PROF cost-share sweep, what did the combined setting PT_PROF=3 (no shadow walk and no mesh closest-hit) measure?
answer: PT_PROF=3 (no shadow walk AND no mesh closest-hit) was never measured — my round-5 sweep only ran the single-bit settings, and those are the numbers on record: full 45.35 ms, bit 1 (skip shadow walk) 44.05 ms (~1.3 ms), bit 4 (skip NEE) 43.17 ms (~2.2 ms), bit 2 (skip mesh closest-hit) 4.77 ms, bit 8 (glass always-reflect) 35.76 ms, all gpu_ms_best at 512x512/64spp in the scratch build in _prof/ (params.pad carries the bitmask, set from the PT_PROF env var in _prof/src/pt_scene.cpp). I know this because the cost-share entry in my working memory, written straight from that sweep, lists exactly those five values and no combined one. The reason I did not need the combination is that bit 2 already dominates: with the mesh walk gone there is essentially nothing left for bit 1 to remove (shadow rays traverse the same BVH/triangle code), so PT_PROF=3 would land at roughly the 4.77 ms figure, and the useful conclusion — that the closest-hit BVH walk is ~89% of the frame and therefore the only place worth optimizing — comes from the single-bit pair 45.35 vs 4.77.
